subject: social-studies
title: Landscape Change: The Singapore River Mouth, Stage by Stage Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says Singapore's landscape changed in one sudden jump, because the fishing village was replaced by the modern city in a single step. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - different pictures mean a sudden change

The change was gradual: the fishing village first became a trading port with godowns and a jetty as trade grew, the port then expanded with warehouses and steamships, and only later did the modern city rise - stage by stage at the same site, with more people living there at every stage.
The city was built in a different place, and the village is still there today
The village and the city stood side by side from the very start

questions.misconception: Singapore's landscape changed in one sudden jump, because the fishing village was replaced by the modern city in a single step.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Singapore's landscape changed in one sudden jump, because the fishing village was replaced by the modern city in a single step. Reteach point: The change was gradual and driven by growing trade: the fishing village first became a trading port with godowns and a jetty, the port then expanded with warehouses and steamships, and only later did the modern city of tall buildings, roads and container ships rise - stage by stage at the same site, with the population growing at every stage.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain what caused the fishing village to become a port.
questions.answer: Growing trade caused it: more ships came, so godowns were built to store goods and a jetty was built for the ships, and people arrived to work at the port.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the driver and the building order: trade grows, godowns and jetty are built, workers arrive.

questions.prompt: In the final stage, the shore at the river mouth holds:

choices.text: Only huts and small fishing boats, exactly as at the start
Tall buildings, busy roads and container ships
An empty beach with no buildings at all
A single godown and nothing else

questions.feedback: Scene 4 shows the modern city on the same shore: tall buildings, busy roads and container ships - the last stage of the gradual change.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the final stage of the change and the stages that came before it.
questions.answer: The final stage is the modern city, and it came after the fishing village became a trading port and the port then expanded with warehouses and steamships.
questions.feedback: A strong answer gives the whole order - fishing village, trading port, expanded port, modern city - with no stage skipped.
